newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steadies with crude, market two-tiered.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steadies with crude, market two-tiered.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices held steady to higher on Monday after crude catapulted more than 60 cents for the expiring January contract.
But traders said the market had become two-tiered, with traders bidding for pipeline spec material near $223 cif, but end-users looking to buy in the physical market closer to $215/$218 cif.
"If you look at the physical market and the fundamentals, the demand is not there," said one source. "The demand is from the traders."
"The reality is that the market is at $223 for 25,000 tonnes of pipeline spec...but if you're trying to sell 10,000 tonnes of paraffinic or heavier N+A or full range, it is at $215," he said.
IPE Brent for Feb and March tacked on more than 80 cents as cold weather forecasts for the Northeast U.S. boosted crude and heating oil prices.
But one end-user said the NWE physical naphtha market remained well supplied, with prices moving close to contango, though concrete bids were scarce.
"The market looks like it's coming into a contango," he said. "Physical material is not being placed."
He said there was material available from Russia and Libya into Northwest Europe, as well as fob material into Rotterdam.
Dec swaps were last heard traded at $219.50 but were believed to have moved higher after crude rallied further, toward $221/$223.
